before: Deletion should specify what disappears and what survives. Removing an unknown ID leaves the contents unchanged under this contract.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
filter keeps records whose predicate is true. !== keeps every ID except the selected one. filter returns a new array without changing the input array.

Read the function call removeNote([{"id":1},{"id":2},{"id":3}], 2) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, removeNote runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
The requested ID is absent. What should this helper return? Every existing record passes the not-equal predicate, so all survive.
after: Removing a note should affect the selected ID only. Every other note should keep its content and position relative to the others.
filter builds a new array from items that pass its test. note.id !== id keeps a note when its ID does not exactly match the requested one.
filter does not change the original array. The kept note objects are reused, so this function must not edit their fields.
If no ID matches, every existing note passes the keep test. The result is a new array containing all the same notes. An empty input gives an empty result.
Complete removeNote(notes, id). Keep notes with different IDs and leave out matching ones. Do not remove by array position or change either input.
